text.p: At least 13 people were killed when a gas explosion blew up an apartment block in northwest Russia and one person was missing in the rubble, rescue officials said on Saturday.
The blast in the town of Priozersk, 120 km (80 miles) north of St Petersburg, on Friday was so powerful that parts of the roof of the five-storey building fell through to the ground floor.
Nearly 500 rescuers from Russia and a small group from Finland worked throughout an extremely cold day on Saturday to remove bodies and debris.
"It's horrible, just indescribable," doctor Andrei Chertilov told NTV. "The last body pulled out was just like a photograph imprinted on a mattress. Hit by two blocks, she died instantly."
Larisa Gonchar, a duty officer at the rescue headquarters, said 65 people survived the explosion.
A police spokesman, quoted by Interfax news agency, blamed illegal tapping into the gas supply system for the blast.
He said a family living in one of the flats had its gas cut off for unpaid bills in March and cut into the gas main "in a flagrant breach of safety regulations" when cold weather returned.
Alexander Yefremov, chief of the civil defence headquarters, told NTV: "We are inclined to think it was a gas explosion. How exactly it happened will be looked into by a special commission."
